sections.overview: The sharp-tailed grouse is a North American grouse found in open habitats from Alaska and Canada into parts of the western and north-central United States.
sections.identification: Its pointed tail and feathered legs help distinguish this grouse.
sections.habitat: Depending on the subspecies, it occupies grasslands, shrub-steppe, open woodland edges and brushy openings.
sections.diet: Its diet is largely plant-based, with insects also important for young birds.
sections.behavior: Males gather on open leks and perform energetic courtship displays.
sections.reproduction: Females nest on the ground, and the chicks leave the nest soon after hatching.
sections.ecology: It shares the genus Tympanuchus with the greater and lesser prairie-chickens; the sharp-tailed grouse uses a wider mix of grassland and shrub habitats.
sections.conservation: Canadian monitoring suggests little overall change in its population since about 1970.
